name: The Foster household — a name from the post office's letter lists
head: foster_caleb

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RETURN, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The office's list of letters uncalled-for is a RETURN — its statement of what was still unclaimed on ONE day — and the paper reprinted one return over as many consecutive issues as it took, so the bound is dated by the return of 1 January 1834 and not by the issue it was read in (T-0425). The earliest issue this project reads the name in is 1834-01-28, 27 days later; that gap is an accident of which impression an extraction pass reached, and it is not evidence. Somebody was writing to this name at Chicago by 1834-01-01 and at no stated time before it; nothing says when they came. The date lines the printings set, and how they were weighed, stand beside this rule in tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py.

lives_at.note: Not attested: a letter list gives a name and no address.

works_at.note: Not attested. No trade is recorded, so there is no premises to seek.

last_dated_appearance.note: A DATED READING OF THIS PERSON, AND THE LAST ONE THE CORPUS HOLDS. Read from `letter_list_returns` as `1835-05-20`, which reaches 1835-05-20 — 42 day(s) short of 1835-07-01. A RETURN IS A DATE AND NOT A CITATION: `letter_list_returns` carries no source per return, so this leg cites none and the corpus that printed it is named in the person's own `sources`. THE FIELD IS THE EVIDENCE UNDER THE VERDICT, not a new claim: nothing here moves the presence off `uncertain`, and T-1159 and T-1172 classify this household by this date instead of reading it out of the prose (T-1144 acceptance 9).

present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Nothing after 1835-05-20 follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

occupation.note: No source records an occupation for this person. A list of uncalled-for letters prints a name and no trade, and this pass will not read one in.

persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, AND HELD THERE MORE THAN ONCE. The papers print 'Caleb Foster' and 'Foster, Culeb' in 2 separate returns of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 28 January 1834, column 1; the Democrat of 20 May 1835, column 13 — across 1834-01-28 to 1835-05-20. A name in a LATER return is somebody still being written to, months on, which is the strongest thing a letter list can say about residence and is why this person outranks a single-return name of the same surname. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

resident_research.evidence_for: No reliable record found in the reviewed contemporary, institutional, local-history and index searches could be tied to this person by more than the recorded name. This is a documented no-find, not evidence that the person did not exist.
resident_research.notes: Candidate facts remain unasserted until a source bridges the candidate to the historical record by more than name similarity.
resident_research.summary: Nothing reviewed in this pass corroborates Caleb Foster from outside the record already held: the chicago tribune 1882 04 25 old settler deaths, fergus chicago directory 1843, norris directory 1844 agreement is a surname-only refusal; the papers hold the name only on the post-office return(s) of 1834-01-28 to 1835-05-20, 1835-08-19.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.

surname_collision.refusal: the town already names a Foster
surname_collision.note: A COLLISION SAID, NOT ACTED ON. Run against the tree as it stands, this pass would not MINT this card: refusal 7 — 'the town already names a Foster' — lands on it, because Amos Foster (hh_foster_amos); John N Foster (hh_foster_john_n) already holds the family name Foster. The owner ruled on 2026-09-18 (T-0660, option (c)) that refusals 7 and 8 are MINT-TIME rules: they decide whether a new household may be minted on a family name the town already spends, and they do not un-mint one that already stands. So this record is not retired, its id is not redirected at anybody, the town's population does not move, and the research row and directory matches it carries are not stranded on a retirement nothing draws. What has changed is that the collision is legible: a reader sees both cards and why both are here. REFUSAL 7 IS NOT A CLAIM THAT TWO RECORDS ARE ONE PERSON — it is the precedence rule between this pass and the ones above it, which give a man the papers gave a trade the family name a letter list only spells. Two of the collisions this reading uncovered are two different men. The pass's `rank()` is unchanged and the cohort is not re-derived; that was option (b)'s cost and the ruling declined to pay it. The derivation behind this block, both readings side by side, is docs/RESEARCH/letter-list-surname-collisions.md.
